definition_sources.name: LuxAlgo library: Break of Structure
what_it_says: A break of structure is a with-trend structural break: in an uptrend, price trading through the most recent significant swing high; in a downtrend, through the most recent swing low. The counter-trend equivalent is a change of character.
Some sources use BOS loosely for any structural break.
Confirmation conventions vary: many traders require a candle body to close beyond the swing; wick-based readings react earlier and mislabel more sweeps.
A change of character is also called a market structure shift by many traders; usage varies by author.
FAQ: not all breaks lead to continuation, and most BOS-based models do not buy the break itself but wait for a retracement.
not_specified: how many bars define a swing
how trend is established in numbers

definition_sources.name: LuxAlgo library: Swing High/low
what_it_says: A swing high is a bar whose high stands above the highs of a set number of bars on either side; that number is the only parameter, and there is no universal setting.
A swing point cannot be confirmed until the right-side bars have closed: a swing high with strength 5 is only knowable five bars after it printed.

definition_sources.name: TMGM academy: Break of Structure (BOS)
what_it_says: A BOS occurs when price moves beyond a significant previous swing high or low in the direction of an existing trend.
BOS is commonly associated with Smart Money Concepts and Inner Circle Trader (ICT) terminology; the underlying principle also belongs to traditional price action analysis.
Swing points can be defined by a specified number of completed candles on each side; no single swing-selection method is universally required, and no number is given.
Changing the definition after observing the outcome introduces hindsight bias.
Describes both a breakout entry (after a confirmed close) and a retest entry; BOS is not a guaranteed trading signal.
not_specified: number of candles on each side
